title: Efforts to Drive Support for New Shared Parental Leave Scheme and Commencement Date for Scheme
what_it_is: Efforts to Drive Support for New Shared Parental Leave Scheme and Commencement Date for Scheme

sections.label: Shared Parental Leave scheme details
sections.summary: The Shared Parental Leave scheme provides 10 additional weeks of paid leave shareable between both parents, with implementation set for 1 April 2025 after tripartite consultation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The new Shared Parental Leave (SPL) scheme is a significant enhancement of our parental leave provisions, providing 10 additional weeks of paid leave that can be shared between both parents to care for their infant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The implementation date of 1 April 2025 was set after extensive consultation with the tripartite partners.

sections.label: Support for parents before April 2025
sections.summary: The implementation date cannot be brought forward, but parents of babies born before 1 April 2025 remain eligible for Marriage and Parenthood package support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As such, we are not able to bring forward the implementation date.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Parents whose babies are born before 1 April 2025 will still be eligible for comprehensive support under the Marriage and Parenthood package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: These include the recent enhancements to the Baby Bonus Scheme that provides for higher financial support, as well as the doubling of Government-Paid Paternity Leave, on a voluntary basis, and Unpaid Infant Care Leave since 1 January 2024 to give parents more time to care for their newborn or to settle caregiving arrangements.

sections.label: Employers' wait-and-see approach
sections.summary: Some employers may adopt a wait-and-see approach, but Shared Parental Leave becomes mandatory on 1 April 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In fact, I think the point Ms Soh made was that some employers may not be acting proactively, they may adopt a wait-and-see approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But what employers should bear in mind is that come 1 April 2025, it is mandatory, it comes into effect.

sections.label: Government-Paid Parental Leave funding
sections.summary: Shared Parental Leave is Government-Paid, so employers do not bear the salary during the employee's leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The first thing to remember is that this is Government-Paid Parental Leave, or Shared Parental Leave, which means that the employers do not have to bear the salary for the period when the employee is on Shared Parental Leave.

sections.label: Extra pay for covering colleagues
sections.summary: One possible solution is to pay extra those who cover for colleagues, as they carry an additional load.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Another possible solution would be, those who have to cover for their colleagues, you could pay them extra, which is fair, because they are carrying an additional load.

sections.label: Productivity Solutions Grant access
sections.summary: They can tap on the Productivity Solutions Grant and other grants made available by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For those, they can tap on things like the Productivity Solutions Grant and all the other grants that the Government has made available.
